title: Application of Negotiated Programme Rates to Company Bookings
content:
Under the Corporate Travel Programmes, the negotiated air, hotel and car discounts of the tier are applied to the published price of a booking made under the programme, and they replace every consumer concession rather than adding to them.

## The basis the discount acts on

A negotiated discount is applied before taxes and third-party fees and never after. The basis it acts on is the published price before taxes and third-party fees.

## Where a supplier's promotional price is lower

Where a supplier's own promotional price is lower than the negotiated price, the lower of the two is taken and the negotiated discount is not applied on top.

## Club points and waivers on a programme booking

A traveller booking under the programme earns no personal club points and takes no personal club fee waiver on that booking, whatever tier they hold; a tier that permits pooling lets the company collect those points into a company pool instead.

## Preferred supplier rates

Preferred supplier rates are reached only by the tiers that carry preferred access, and a tier without it books at published rates less its negotiated discount.

## A booking made outside the programme

A booking made outside the programme by a traveller who holds a seat is a private booking, priced on consumer terms, and is never billed to the company.

## Worked illustration, on hypothetical figures

Take a published air fare of 1000.00 USD before taxes and third-party fees, on a programme whose negotiated air discount is 20 per cent. Twenty per cent of 1000.00 USD is 200.00 USD, so the negotiated price is 800.00 USD, and taxes and third-party fees are added to that figure afterwards rather than before it.

Take the same fare where the supplier's own promotional price stands at 750.00 USD before taxes and third-party fees. The promotional price is the lower of the two, so 750.00 USD is the price taken, and the negotiated discount of 20 per cent is not applied to it as well.

## Points of judgement

**A traveller who holds a Wanderlane Traveller Club membership books under the programme and asks for their points.** No personal club points are earned on a booking made under the programme and no personal club fee waiver is taken on it, whatever club tier that traveller holds. On a programme tier that permits pooling, the company collects those points into a company pool instead.

**A consumer concession is advertised on a fare the programme has negotiated.** The negotiated discount replaces that concession rather than adding to it.

**A traveller who holds a seat books a holiday of their own outside the programme.** That is a private booking, priced on consumer terms, and it is never billed to the company.
